figures.finding: From 1 January 2026 an individual's taxable income (after reliefs) is taxed at 0% on the first NGN 800,000, then 15%, 18%, 21%, 23% and 25% above NGN 50 million; the rates are national, collected by the State Internal Revenue Service where the person lives.

value.administeredBy: Nigeria Revenue Service or the Internal Revenue Service of a State or the FCT

figures.applies: Nigeria Tax Act 2025, Fourth Schedule, in force from 1 January 2026; employment income at or below the National Minimum Wage is exempt.

"relevant tax authority" means Nigeria Revenue Service, the Internal Revenue Service of a State or the Federal Capital Territory in Nigeria

figures.finding: There is no flat allowance beyond the 0% band; eligible deductions are the individual's National Housing Fund, health insurance and pension contributions, mortgage interest on an owner-occupied home, life insurance premiums, and rent relief of 20% of rent paid up to NGN 500,000.

sources.said: (i) the individual's contributions under the National Housing Fund, (ii) the individual's contributions under the National Health Insurance Scheme, (iii) the individual's contributions under the Pension Reform Act,

figures.finding: The year of assessment is the calendar year; employers file their employees' emolument return by 31 January; the Act sets no explicit date for an individual's own return, and the state tax authorities set 31 March (Edo State's notice for 2026 names 31 January for employers and 31 March for all other taxable persons).
figures.applies: From 2026; the 31 March date is read from the Edo State Internal Revenue Service's notice citing NTAA 2025 ss. 13-14 (the relevant tax authority for a resident individual is the state of residence; other states' notices not read).

sources.said: "year of assessment" means government tax year being 1st of January to 31 of December of any year.

An employer shall file a return with the relevant tax authority for all emoluments paid to its employees, not later than 31 January of each year in respect of all employees in its employment in the preceding year.

Pursuant to Section 14 subsections (1), (2) & (3), Section 13 subsection (1) & (2) of the Nigerian Tax Administration Act (NTAA) 2025, & Section 26 of the Nigeria Tax Act (NTA) 2025, the Edo State Internal Revenue Service (EIRS), hereby notifies all employers of labour and all taxable persons in Edo State to file their 2026 Annual Tax Returns not later than 31st of January, 2026 and 31st of March, 2026 respectively.

figures.finding: Under the contributory pension scheme the employer pays at least 10% and the employee 8% of monthly emoluments (or the employer at least 20% alone).

pension.base: monthly emoluments (not less than basic, housing and transport)

figures.applies: Pension Reform Act 2014 s 4 (per PwC's 2014 summary); NHF, NSITF and any performers' scheme not read.

sources.said: The rates of contributions to be made under the new Scheme by both the employer and employee are a minimum of 10% and 8% respectively

figures.finding: The employer deducts income tax from emoluments so that the year's deductions equal the tax chargeable (PAYE); a payer of fees deducts tax at source at the rate set by regulation (for consultancy and professional fees to an individual, 5% resident and 10% non-resident under the 2024 regulations).

value.employee: PAYE: cumulative deduction equal to annual tax

figures.applies: NTAA 2025 s 51 defers rates to the deduction-at-source regulations; the 2024 regulations' rates are read from PwC's summary, and whether they carry over unchanged into 2026 was not confirmed.

sources.said: In arriving at the amount of income tax to be deducted from any payment of or on account of the emolument to an employee, the employer shall ensure that the aggregate amount of all the deductions made during a year of assessment shall equal the income tax chargeable on the employee in respect of its emoluments for that year.

Where any payment is made to a person, the person making the payment shall, at the date when payment is made or otherwise settled, deduct the tax at the rate prescribed in regulations relating to deduction of tax at source.

figures.finding: VAT is 7.5%; a small business (turnover of NGN 50 million or less, fixed assets under NGN 250 million, and not providing professional services) is exempt from registering, charging and filing.
figures.applies: From 2026; whether a freelance screen worker counts as 'professional services' is not settled by the text read.

sources.said: VAT shall be charged on the value of all taxable supplies at the rate of 7.5%.

"small business" means a business that earns gross turnover of N50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets less than N250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business
choose to opt out of the exemption granted to small businesses under this Part including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns.
